rows.desktop_responsibility: Define the Host extension composition contract: immutable extension declarations and dependency lists, deterministic dependency-ordered boot, duplicate/missing/self/cycle rejection, dependency API injection, event fan-out failure reporting, reverse-order teardown, and rollback of already-started extensions when a later start fails.
rows.desktop_visible_effect: Shipping Host extensions start only after declared peers, fail deterministically on invalid graphs, and unwind already-started resources in reverse order on startup failure or stop.
rows.ios_platform_delta: iOS statically composes the native Rust AppHost/FeatureHost and does not load the Desktop TypeScript extension graph. Existing Rust builders/runtime shutdown paths provide portions of composition/lifecycle ownership, but this review did not find one canonical iOS contract that proves duplicate/missing/cycle validation plus reverse teardown/rollback semantics equivalent to this source.
rows.production_evidence: Current shipping owner candidates are the repository-owned Rust AppHost/Host/Runtime composition. Evidence is insufficient to claim full extension-graph parity because no canonical dynamic/static graph contract covering all Desktop invariants has been identified.
rows.test_evidence: Current Rust Host/AppHost tests cover many individual composition paths, but no focused current-head contract was found for the complete Desktop extension DAG + rollback semantics.
rows.notes: Current Desktop 8148bfb9 blob reviewed. Explicit architecture gap retained rather than marking the TypeScript mechanism N/A without proving its lifecycle responsibilities are preserved.
rows.exact_head_evidence: responsibility reviewed; canonical replacement contract and exact-head evidence pending

rows.desktop_responsibility: Provide shared scheduling policies with strict parameter validation and cancellation semantics: wall/monotonic clock, deadline with deadline_exceeded error and child abort, bounded exponential retry with shouldRetry, keyed expiry, non-overlapping polling, idle watchdog, debounce, disposable timers and AbortSignal propagation.
rows.desktop_visible_effect: Timeouts, retries, expiry, polling, watchdog and debounce behave consistently, cancel promptly, avoid stale callbacks, and expose deterministic deadline failures across runtime callers.
rows.ios_platform_delta: Native iOS currently implements caller-specific retry, timeout, generation fencing and cancellation in Gateway, Remote Computer, Host supervision, automations and Rust runtime code. Those local owners preserve portions of the behavior, but no single reviewed native policy layer or caller-complete audit yet proves all Desktop scheduling contracts (deadline error shape, keyed expiry, non-overlapping polling, watchdog and debounce).
rows.production_evidence: Examples of real shipping scheduling semantics include GatewayRetryPolicy/cancellation, CoordinatorHostSupervisor generation fencing, RemoteComputer deadline races, and native automation scheduling. Aggregate caller coverage is not yet sufficient to promote the shared responsibility.
rows.test_evidence: Existing focused tests cover individual retry/deadline/cancellation owners; a full current-main caller audit and any missing policy tests remain required.
rows.notes: Current Desktop 8148bfb9 blob reviewed. This row records an explicit aggregate scheduling-coverage gap rather than inferring parity from scattered timer usage.
rows.exact_head_evidence: responsibility reviewed; aggregate native scheduling closure and exact-head evidence pending
